body:
N-48 measurement plan, 26 Nov 2026 (lead, with the advisor's frame). MEASURE, DO NOT BUILD: no production code and no tests of a discography round until the numbers are read and the product ruling on single_only is made.

FACTS CHECKED IN THE REPO (not assumed): (1) the catalogue already has an artist-albums call: `Catalogue.artist_page(artist_id, ("releases",))` -> `GET /artist/{id}/albums?limit=200` (RELEASES_LIMIT = 200), rows carry id, title, record_type (album, ep, single...), release_date, explicit_lyrics, NO tracks and NO ISRC; the recorded answer has `total` and `next` (pagination by `index`, 83 releases for an artist whose first page held 50), so an artist with more than 200 releases needs more pages. (2) An album's track list (`GET /album/{id}/tracks`) DOES carry `isrc`, `artist`, `track_position`, `disk_number`, and the album object carries `label`, `upc`, `nb_tracks`, `record_type`, `release_date`, `contributors`: so ISRC-first matching is possible, and `label` and `upc` are two more signals to MEASURE (not trust). (3) Cost: 1 request per artist for the list + 1 per album whose tracks are read, so the exclusivity signal (below) needs the track list of ALL the artist's albums: O(albums) per artist; with about 90 artists holding the 135 held songs and about 20 albums each that is about 2,000 requests, the size of one live dry run (1,429 on 26 Nov).

THE MEASUREMENT (extend `album_dryrun`, read-only, recorded and replayable, `--live --max-requests`): for each held song (single_only 32, sole_album 49, date_decided 24-26, single_before_album 27, compilation_title 3 on the 672-song library): take the artist id from the same-recording hits (never from the name); fetch the artist's release list, then the track lists of its albums and EPs; record whether any non-single release carries the recording (ISRC first, then the existing title/version/length judge), how many release families carry it, each carrying release's date, label and upc, and the requests spent; for each carrying release the SHARE OF ITS TRACKS WHOSE ISRC APPEARS ON ANOTHER OF THE ARTIST'S RELEASES (an original's tracks are mostly its own; a best-of's are mostly found elsewhere: the only compilation signal that needs neither dates nor English words).

THE LABELED SET (a fixture, written FIRST; a rule is judged against it): the FIVE wrong stamps of 25 Nov (Always On Time -> Wonderful, Hotel -> Hotel, Welcome to the Black Parade -> May Death Never Stop You, Break Stuff -> Greatest Hitz, All The Small Things -> I Won't Be Home For Christmas); the held controls with their real albums (Stankonia, Hybrid Theory, Numb, Breaking the Habit, Meteora x2); the 41 good stamps (local/n34-dryrun-24nov/matched_ids_report3.txt); the two album tracks wrongly left as singles (What's Luv?, Buy U A Drank). A rule passes only if it yields NONE of the five, keeps ALL 41 and recovers the controls.

FIRST RUN: the labeled set plus about 30 held songs with a tight cap; read it; then the full run.

THE FOUR QUESTIONS THE NUMBERS MUST ANSWER: (a) RECOVERY: how many songs per hold reason get exactly one non-compilation home; (b) SAFETY: does the exclusivity signal separate the labeled set; (c) COST: requests per artist, and how much one discography covers; (d) YEAR: do discography dates give the real years (Weathered 2001, The Invisible Band 2001, Contraband 2004)? EXPECTED NO (the same reissue dates): then the trigger of the 'no year in a stamp' stop-gap (comment in album_finder.choose_release, docs/18, CHANGELOG, board) that points at N-48 is FALSE TEXT and must be re-pointed honestly; any other source of a year is a new outside service = a PRIVACY.md change and a decision.

PRODUCT RULING TO BRING WITH THE NUMBERS (not decided here): may `single_only` become a single stamp once the discography proves no album carries the recording?
